context:
Goal: a ruling of yours governs every session and every guard from the moment you make it, not hours later when main takes it in (your question, 14:28 CST).
Problem (rule): a ruling lives off main until a lane rewrites the rule and its batch merges; running sessions loaded the rules file at start and the guards run main's code, so both keep enforcing the old rule.
Based on (measured): main has not moved since 09:09 CST, and batch 104 sat green from 14:04 CST.
Based on (read): the timer miss at 14:15 CST and the round-3 miss at 14:24 CST both cited main's old text over the restart plan.
Departs from: main — guards obey only main's code — one ruling store can lift a named guard rule before its code lands.
home: step ruled-store-one-home (one store for rulings not yet on main)

options.gain: Guards stay code-only; a ruling never loosens a guard before its code is reviewed.
options.how: Rulings govern prose and the past-ruling checks only; a guard keeps refusing until its code merges. Pair it with step ruled-prose-express so a ruled change reaches main faster.
options.label: Rulings govern text only (Recommended)
options.lose: You keep typing override, or waiting, on every ruled change to a hook until it merges.

options.gain: A ruling holds everywhere within one turn, guards included, with no override typing.
options.how: Only triage writes the store, from your quoted words with their time; each lift names one guard rule; the entry closes when main takes the change in. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. Retrospective: possible false alarm; this is the owner's override made lasting, not a per-repo form.
options.label: Your ruling governs the guard now
options.lose: The store becomes a second form the guards accept: a wrong entry lifts a guard until someone notices.

short: Rulings off main: guards too, or text only
title: Does a ruling not yet on main also govern the guards?
why: Today a ruling waits for main before guards and running sessions obey it.
